originalTitle: High Dividend ETFs Are Beating the S&P 500 Again in 2026 and These 3 Pay Over 3 Percent While Doing It
summary: Growth stocks dominated for years, but 2026 has handed dividend ETFs an unexpected edge, and three funds yielding over 3% are proving the rotation is real. The question is whether you own the right one for what comes next.
content:
Growth stocks dominated for years, but 2026 has handed dividend ETFs an unexpected edge, and three funds yielding over 3% are proving the rotation is real. The question is whether you own the right one for what comes next.

The ETF Examiner desk. Editor: Ryne Mauck .

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Dividend investors have watched growth names lead the market for years, but 2026 has flipped that script. The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF ( NYSEARCA:SCHD ), the iShares Core High Dividend ETF ( NYSEARCA:HDV ), and the Schwab International Dividend Equity ETF ( NYSEARCA:SCHY ) all pay yields north of 3%, and two of the three are running well ahead of the S&P 500 through late September.

The S&P 500 is up 13% year-to-date on a price basis. SCHD is up 24%, HDV is up 19%, and SCHY, the international counterpart, is up 9%. The three funds cover different corners of the dividend world, and picking between them comes down to what problem you are trying to solve.

Why Dividend Payers Are Winning Again

After a long stretch when mega-cap growth crowded out everything else, capital has rotated this year toward cash-generative businesses trading at reasonable multiples. Healthcare, staples, energy, and industrials — sectors dividend indexes lean into — have carried the rally. That rotation is showing up cleanly in fund performance rather than in a handful of individual winners, which is why comparing screened dividend baskets against the cap-weighted index is especially meaningful right now.

SCHD: The Quality-Dividend Flagship Doing the Heavy Lifting

SCHD is the strongest choice on this list for most investors, and the numbers explain why. It tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, which screens for companies with at least a decade of consecutive dividend payments and then ranks them by cash-flow-to-debt, return on equity, dividend yield, and five-year dividend growth. The result is a portfolio built around durable balance sheets rather than the highest nominal yields.

The fund holds roughly $94.9 billion in net assets, charges 0.06% annually, and carries a 30-day SEC yield of 3.3%. Top positions include QUALCOMM at 7%, Texas Instruments at 6%, and UnitedHealth Group at 5%, with Coca-Cola, Merck, Chevron, Verizon, and Procter & Gamble rounding out the top ten. That is a portfolio designed to pay you while you wait, without the yield traps that plague higher-payout screens.

The tradeoff worth understanding: SCHD’s methodology reconstitutes once a year, which means the fund can carry outsized weights in a handful of sectors between rebalancings. Its underweight in mega-cap technology has been a drag during AI-driven rallies, and it will lag if the market narrows back toward growth leadership. What you are buying is a value tilt with quality guardrails.

HDV: A Higher Yield With a Defensive Moat Screen

HDV takes a different route to the same destination. BlackRock’s fund tracks the Morningstar Dividend Yield Focus Index, which starts with companies that Morningstar’s analysts have rated as having wide or narrow economic moats, then screens for financial health, and selects the highest-yielding names. The moat filter matters here. It biases the portfolio toward businesses with pricing power and defensible competitive positions, which is why energy majors, integrated pharma, and consumer staples dominate.

The expense ratio sits at 0.08%, and the 30-day SEC yield of 3.3% edges out SCHD. HDV has returned 19% year-to-date, comfortably ahead of the S&P 500 but behind its Schwab counterpart. HDV runs a more concentrated portfolio than SCHD, typically holding around 75 names with meaningful weights in the top ten. That concentration is the source of both its yield advantage and its risk profile: a single bad quarter from a major energy or pharma holding hurts HDV more than it would hurt a broader dividend basket.

HDV suits investors who want a check every quarter and are comfortable with a more defensive, sector-tilted portfolio. It has outperformed SCHD during periods when energy and healthcare lead, and underperformed when technology takes over.

SCHY: The Overlooked International Angle

SCHY is the fund most readers will overlook, and that is precisely why it deserves attention. Schwab designed it as the international counterpart to SCHD, tracking the Dow Jones International Dividend 100 Index using the same cash-flow-to-debt and dividend-growth screens applied to non-U.S. developed and emerging markets. The expense ratio matches HDV at 0.08%, and the fund pays a distribution yield near 3.3%.

The portfolio holds $2.3 billion in assets across roughly 100 names spanning Europe, Australia, Canada, Asia, and select emerging markets. Top weights include BHP Group at 5%, Eni at 5%, TotalEnergies at 5%, Deutsche Post at 4%, and Allianz at 4%, with British American Tobacco, Roche, GSK, Unilever, and Vinci also in the top tier. This represents genuine geographic diversification.

The tradeoff: SCHY’s 9% price return lags both its U.S. siblings and the S&P 500 this year. The case for holding it is not near-term outperformance but structural diversification. International dividend payers trade at persistently lower multiples than U.S. equivalents, currency exposure works both ways over long horizons, and dollar weakness would flip the relative return math quickly. For a portfolio already concentrated in U.S. large caps, SCHY adds yield from a different opportunity set.

If you can only own one dividend ETF, SCHD is the default. It has the lowest fee, the strongest 2026 return, the largest asset base, and a methodology that balances yield against quality without leaning too far in either direction.

HDV fits investors who prioritize current income and want a defensive tilt through pharma, staples, and energy. It carries the highest headline yield of the three
chineseTitle: 高股息 ETF 将于 2026 年再次跑赢标准普尔 500 指数，这三只 ETF 的股息率超过 3%
chineseSummary: 成长型股票多年来一直占据主导地位，但 2026 年股息 ETF 获得了意想不到的优势，三只收益率超过 3% 的基金证明了这种轮动是真实的。问题是您是否拥有适合接下来发生的事情的产品。
chineseContent:
成长型股票多年来一直占据主导地位，但 2026 年股息 ETF 获得了意想不到的优势，三只收益率超过 3% 的基金证明了这种轮动是真实的。问题是您是否拥有适合接下来发生的事情的产品。

ETF 审查员柜台。编辑：莱恩·莫克。

这篇文章可能包含来自我们的赞助商和附属机构的链接，Flywheel Publishing 可能会因通过他们采取的行动而获得补偿。

多年来，股息投资者一直看着成长型股票引领市场，但 2026 年扭转了这一局面。 Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (NYSEARCA:SCHD)、iShares Core High Dividend ETF (NYSEARCA:HDV) 和 Schwab International Dividend Equity ETF (NYSEARCA:SCHY) 的收益率均超过 3%，截至 9 月底，这三者中的两家的收益率远远领先于标准普尔 500 指数。

标准普尔 500 指数今年迄今已上涨 13%。 SCHD 上涨 24%，HDV 上涨 19%，国际同行 SCHY 上涨 9%。这三只基金涵盖了股息世界的不同角落，在它们之间进行选择取决于您想要解决的问题。

为什么股息支付者再次获胜

在经历了长期巨额增长压倒其他一切之后，今年资本已转向以合理倍数交易的现金生成企业。医疗保健、主食、能源和工业——股息指数所关注的板块——带动了涨势。这种轮动清楚地体现在基金业绩中，而不是少数个别获胜者身上，这就是为什么将经过筛选的股息篮子与上限加权指数进行比较现在特别有意义。

SCHD：质量红利旗舰承担重任

对于大多数投资者而言，SCHD 是此列表中最强的选择，数字解释了原因。它跟踪道琼斯美国股息 100 指数，该指数筛选连续至少十年支付股息的公司，然后根据现金流量债务比、股本回报率、股息收益率和五年股息增长对它们进行排名。结果是围绕持久资产负债表而不是最高名义收益率建立的投资组合。

该基金持有约 949 亿美元的净资产，年利率为 0.06%，30 天 SEC 收益率为 3.3%。排名前列的包括高通（7%）、德州仪器（6%）和联合健康集团（5%），可口可乐、默克、雪佛龙、威瑞森和宝洁也跻身前十。这是一个旨在在您等待时向您付款的投资组合，而不会出现困扰高支付屏幕的收益率陷阱。

这种权衡值得理解：SCHD 的方法每年重新调整一次，这意味着该基金可以在重新平衡期间在少数行业中持有较大的权重。在人工智能驱动的反弹期间，其对大型科技股的减持一直是一个拖累，如果市场收窄回增长领先地位，那么它就会落后。您购买的是带有质量护栏的价值倾斜。

HDV：具有防御护城河的更高产量

HDV 采用不同的路线到达同一目的地。贝莱德的基金追踪晨星股息收益率焦点指数，该指数从晨星分析师评级为拥有宽或窄经济护城河的公司开始，然后筛选财务健康状况，并选择收益最高的公司。护城河过滤器在这里很重要。它将投资组合偏向于具有定价能力和可防御竞争地位的企业，这就是能源巨头、综合制药和消费必需品占据主导地位的原因。

费用率为 0.08%，30 天 SEC 收益率为 3.3%，略高于 SCHD。 HDV 今年迄今的回报率为 19%，明显领先于标准普尔 500 指数，但落后于嘉信理财指数。 HDV 运营的投资组合比 SCHD 更集中，通常持有大约 75 个名字，在前十名中具有有意义的权重。这种集中度是其收益率优势和风险状况的来源：主要能源或制药控股公司的一个糟糕季度对 HDV 的伤害大于对更广泛的股息篮子的伤害。

HDV 适合那些希望每个季度都有支票并愿意接受更具防御性、偏向行业的投资组合的投资者。在能源和医疗保健领先时期，它的表现优于 SCHD，而在技术占据主导地位时，它的表现则较差。

SCHY：被忽视的国际角度

SCHY 是大多数读者会忽视的基金，这也正是它值得关注的原因。施瓦布将其设计为 SCHD 的国际对应产品，使用适用于非美国发达市场和新兴市场的相同现金流债务比和股息增长屏幕来跟踪道琼斯国际股息 100 指数。 HDV 的费用比率为 0.08%，基金支付的分配收益率接近 3.3%。

该投资组合持有 23 亿美元的资产，涵盖欧洲、澳大利亚、加拿大、亚洲和部分新兴市场的约 100 个名称。权重最高的公司包括必和必拓集团（5%）、埃尼集团（5%）、TotalEnergies（5%）、德国邮政（4%）和安联集团（4%），英美烟草、罗氏（Roche）、葛兰素史克（GSK）、联合利华（Unilever）和芬奇（Vinci）也位列前茅。这代表了真正的地理多元化。

代价是：SCHY 今年 9% 的价格回报率落后于其美国同业指数和标准普尔 500 指数。持有该股的理由不是短期表现优异，而是结构多元化。国际股息支付者的交易市盈率持续低于美国同类公司的市盈率，长期来看，货币风险是双向的，而美元疲软将迅速扭转相对回报率。对于已经集中在美国大盘股的投资组合，SCHY 增加了来自不同机会集的收益率。

如果您只能拥有一只股息 ETF，则默认选择 SCHD。它具有最低的费用、最强的 2026 年回报、最大的资产基础，以及平衡收益与质量而又不会过度偏向任一方向的方法。

HDV 适合那些优先考虑当前收入并希望通过制药、主食和能源进行防御性倾斜的投资者。它的总体收益率是三者中最高的
